<p class="hero-bio">
I am a Ph.D. student in the Department of Agricultural and Applied Economics at Texas Tech University and a Research Assistant at the Free Market Institute. I also serve as a Graduate Instructor in the Area of Energy Commerce & Business Economics at the Rawls College of Business.
</p>

<p class="hero-bio">
My research focuses on migration, entrepreneurship, and political economy, with an emphasis on how institutions, policy environments, and economic incentives influence individual behavior and long-run development outcomes.
</p>

<div class="featured-cards">

<div class="featured-card">
<span class="topic-label topic-migration">Migration</span>
<h4>Did the Syrian Refugee Crisis impact European economic freedom?</h4>
<p class="featured-meta">with Benjamin Powell | Working Paper</p>
<p class="featured-desc">Using the synthetic control method, we find that the Syrian refugee surge did not meaningfully impact economic freedom in Germany, Austria, or Sweden, despite the largest institutional gap and refugee inflows in modern European history.</p>
<a href="explore-research.html" class="featured-link">Read more &rarr;</a>
</div>

<div class="featured-card">
<span class="topic-label topic-entrepreneurship">Entrepreneurship</span>
<h4>Do corruption reforms spur entrepreneurship?</h4>
<p class="featured-meta">Working Paper</p>
<p class="featured-desc">Applying the Callaway and Sant'Anna (2021) DiD estimator, this paper finds that sustained anti-corruption reforms have no significant effect on entrepreneurship, suggesting the growth benefits of reforms flow through other channels.</p>
<a href="explore-research.html" class="featured-link">Read more &rarr;</a>
